text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc is asking the French and British governments to extend its operating licence by "tens of years" French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle said on Monday.
Eurotunnel's current licence runs for 65 years and expires in 2052. It was extended in December 1993 by 10 years .
He told a news conference shareholders' "sacrifices" being made in Eurotunnel's debt restructuring would be "lightened" if the states extended its concession for the Tunnel.

The two Paris court-appointed mediators have also told the governments an extension would help gain approval by shareholders and the firm's 225 lending banks of a restructuring of its 69.6 billion francs of debt, Eurotunnel said.
Eurotunnel would grant current shareholders a free share warrant for every eight share held if its franchise were extended, it said in a statement.
The warrants would be exercisable before December 31, 2001, at 10.40 francs per share.
If the warrants were all taken up, shareholders would hold around 55.5 percent of Eurotunnel's capital, the company said.
Ponsolle said the government's response was not yet known but the answer should come in the next few weeks.
